lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Hi Keisha, it's Kendra from the coaching program. Is now still a good time?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hi, sorry, I'm in the car but I can talk.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Here's what I had in mind for today, but tell me if you'd rather focus on something else.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Actually, I had a question about what to eat at parties.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How are you doing, really?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: So-so. Up and down.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Did you hit your goal this week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Some days yes, some days no. Maybe 1.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're weighing it up, and that's fair.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: My diabetes is why I'm doing this.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you mind if I tell you what some people do?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes, please.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Keeping the phone out of the bedroom helps a lot of people fall asleep faster.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Got it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay, this week I'll really do it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: This is about more than the drinks on the weekend. It's about getting your life back.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I put a reminder on the fridge.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: If you don't do this, your health is going to suffer.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're still figuring out what works.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I guess.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're open to it. You just want it to fit your real life.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What would your family say about these changes?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'm not sure.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's been a mixed week.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I don't know.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You'd rather start small and actually stick with it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I already told my family about my goal.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Come on, you can find 10 minutes.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're weighing it up, and that's fair.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'd like to be able to keep up with my grandkids.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You have to make this a priority.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I guess.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You need to be in bed by ten, period.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Next week I want you to be in bed by 10:30 on 4 nights.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah, but you don't know my schedule.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: On a scale of 0 to 10, how confident are you that you can do that?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: 5. Maybe 6.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Why a 5 and not a 2?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I feel better about myself when I stick to it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: If getting started gets in the way again, what's your backup plan?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I mean, if it rains I'll walk in the hallway of my building.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: I'll text you midweek to see how it's going, and we'll talk again in two weeks.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: That works.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay Keisha, have a good rest of your day.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Thanks, bye bye.

tags.note: Asks how to handle party eating
Invites check-in on how she is
Phone tip, weakly linked to her goal
Assumes weekend drinks issue she never raised
Took a concrete step, fridge reminder
Reflects openness and need for fit
Has already shared goal with family
Feels better when sticking to it

flags.reason: Health warning pushes change without permission, a MI-inconsistent move.
Pressure to find 10 minutes ignores the participant's stated schedule barriers.
Grandkids motivation at line 34 was met with a directive rather than exploration.
Absolute 'period' directive undermines autonomy and partnership.
Sets 10:30 target unilaterally, then participant pushes back at line 40 without the coach exploring it.

score.summary: The coach opened collaboratively and used good follow-up questions on confidence and backup planning, but repeatedly shifted into directives and warnings (lines 19, 31, 35, 37, 39) that overrode the participant's stated barriers and motivation. The participant's change talk around grandkids and family support was not built on, and the goal was imposed rather than co-created.
strengths: Line 3 offered a collaborative agenda and invited the participant to redirect.
Line 43 asked 'Why a 5 and not a 2?', which drew out reasons for change.
Line 45 asked for a backup plan, which the participant answered concretely at line 46.
Line 47 set a clear next contact with a midweek text and a two-week follow-up.
coaching_tips: Line 35 and 37: replace 'You have to' and 'period' with a question, such as 'What would make a bedtime change realistic for you?'
Line 39: after the participant's objection at line 40, ask permission before proposing the 10:30 target, then negotiate it with her.
Line 34: when she named her grandkids, reflect that value ('Keeping up with them matters a lot to you') before moving to action.
Line 17 and 19: drop the warning and the assumed drinks issue; ask what she sees as the biggest concern instead.
